system.description:
Lossoth

Les Lossoth sont les Hommes du Grand Nord établis autour de la baie de Forochel. Leur Culture s’est façonnée dans un pays de toundra, de neige, de glace et de vents violents où la survie dépend d’une connaissance intime des saisons, des animaux et des déplacements sur terrain gelé. Ils appartiennent à la Race Humains — Hildor et restent l’un des peuples les mieux adaptés aux conditions polaires de la Terre du Milieu.

Le Grand Nord

Les communautés lossoth vivent au rythme du gel, des migrations animales et de la disponibilité des ressources. Le campement, l’abri et les itinéraires changent avec les saisons ; les familles savent reconnaître la neige porteuse, la glace dangereuse, les signes d’une tempête et les zones où trouver gibier ou combustible.

Le froid n’est pas un simple décor mais une donnée permanente de la vie. Les vêtements, la nourriture, l’organisation des déplacements et la répartition des tâches sont pensés pour éviter toute dépense inutile de chaleur ou d’énergie.

Apparence et adaptation

Les Lossoth sont généralement robustes et compacts, avec des traits adaptés à un climat extrême. Leurs vêtements superposent peaux, fourrures et cuir afin de protéger le corps du vent et de l’humidité. Leur endurance face au froid est remarquable, tandis que les climats très chauds leur sont beaucoup moins familiers.

Chasse, pêche et élevage

La chasse, la pêche et le piégeage assurent l’essentiel des ressources. Les Lossoth exploitent la viande, les peaux, les os et la graisse avec très peu de gaspillage. Les chiens et les rennes occupent une place importante dans certaines communautés pour le transport, la traction ou l’élevage.

Le savoir pratique vaut autant que la force : suivre une piste après une chute de neige, construire rapidement un abri, conserver de la nourriture ou traverser une étendue gelée sont des compétences ordinaires.

Société et traditions

La famille et le groupe de survie priment sur les institutions complexes. Les anciens sont respectés pour leur mémoire des hivers, des migrations et des lieux sûrs. La parole donnée et l’entraide ont un poids particulier dans un environnement où l’isolement peut être mortel.

Les récits, chants et croyances transmettent la mémoire des ancêtres, des esprits, des animaux et des phénomènes naturels. La religion reste étroitement liée au monde visible et aux forces qui gouvernent le Nord.

Voyage et combat

Les Lossoth excellent dans le déplacement sur neige, le pistage, la survie, l’observation météorologique et l’utilisation d’équipements adaptés au froid. Leurs armes restent fonctionnelles : lances, javelots, arcs, couteaux et outils de chasse dominent. La mobilité et la connaissance du terrain comptent davantage qu’une armure lourde.

Place dans la création de personnage

Un personnage Lossoth est d’abord défini par sa communauté, son territoire de chasse et sa relation au Grand Nord. Un voyage vers le Sud constitue un changement considérable : abondance de bois, routes permanentes, villes et climats doux lui paraissent souvent aussi étranges que la banquise l’est à un Gondorien.

Langues de départ

  • Labba — Parlée 8 / Écrite 0
  • Westron — Parlée 4 / Écrite 2
  • Sindarin — Parlée 4 / Écrite 2

Lossoth

The Lossoth are the Men of the Far North who dwell around the Bay of Forochel. Their Culture was shaped in a land of tundra, snow, ice and violent winds where survival depends on intimate knowledge of the seasons, animals and movement across frozen ground. They belong to the Humans — Hildor Race and remain one of the peoples best adapted to the polar conditions of Middle-earth.

The Far North

Lossoth communities live according to the rhythm of freezing weather, animal migrations and the availability of resources. Camps, shelters and routes change with the seasons; families know how to recognise load-bearing snow, dangerous ice, signs of a storm and areas where game or fuel can be found.

Cold is not merely a background feature but a permanent condition of life. Clothing, food, the organisation of travel and the division of tasks are all designed to avoid wasting heat or energy.

Appearance and adaptation

The Lossoth are generally sturdy and compact, with features adapted to an extreme climate. Their clothing layers hides, fur and leather to protect the body from wind and moisture. Their endurance against cold is remarkable, while very hot climates are far less familiar to them.

Hunting, fishing and husbandry

Hunting, fishing and trapping provide most resources. The Lossoth use meat, hides, bones and fat with very little waste. Dogs and reindeer hold an important place in some communities for transport, hauling or herding.

Practical knowledge matters as much as strength: following a trail after snowfall, rapidly building shelter, preserving food or crossing a frozen expanse are ordinary skills.

Society and traditions

Family and the survival group take precedence over complex institutions. Elders are respected for their memory of winters, migrations and safe places. Keeping one's word and mutual aid carry particular weight in an environment where isolation can be deadly.

Stories, songs and beliefs transmit the memory of ancestors, spirits, animals and natural phenomena. Religion remains closely tied to the visible world and to the forces that govern the North.

Travel and combat

The Lossoth excel at movement across snow, tracking, survival, weather observation and the use of equipment suited to cold. Their weapons remain functional: spears, javelins, bows, knives and hunting tools predominate. Mobility and knowledge of terrain matter more than heavy armour.

Place in character creation

A Lossoth character is defined first by community, hunting territory and relationship with the Far North. A journey south represents an enormous change: abundant timber, permanent roads, cities and mild climates often seem as strange to them as the pack ice does to a Gondorian.

Starting Languages

  • Labba — Spoken 8 / Written 0
  • Westron — Spoken 4 / Written 2
  • Sindarin — Spoken 4 / Written 2

Lossoth

The Lossoth are the Men of the Far North who dwell around the Bay of Forochel. Their Culture was shaped in a land of tundra, snow, ice and violent winds where survival depends on intimate knowledge of the seasons, animals and movement across frozen ground. They belong to the Humans — Hildor Race and remain one of the peoples best adapted to the polar conditions of Middle-earth.

The Far North

Lossoth communities live according to the rhythm of freezing weather, animal migrations and the availability of resources. Camps, shelters and routes change with the seasons; families know how to recognise load-bearing snow, dangerous ice, signs of a storm and areas where game or fuel can be found.

Cold is not merely a background feature but a permanent condition of life. Clothing, food, the organisation of travel and the division of tasks are all designed to avoid wasting heat or energy.

Appearance and adaptation

The Lossoth are generally sturdy and compact, with features adapted to an extreme climate. Their clothing layers hides, fur and leather to protect the body from wind and moisture. Their endurance against cold is remarkable, while very hot climates are far less familiar to them.

Hunting, fishing and husbandry

Hunting, fishing and trapping provide most resources. The Lossoth use meat, hides, bones and fat with very little waste. Dogs and reindeer hold an important place in some communities for transport, hauling or herding.

Practical knowledge matters as much as strength: following a trail after snowfall, rapidly building shelter, preserving food or crossing a frozen expanse are ordinary skills.

Society and traditions

Family and the survival group take precedence over complex institutions. Elders are respected for their memory of winters, migrations and safe places. Keeping one's word and mutual aid carry particular weight in an environment where isolation can be deadly.

Stories, songs and beliefs transmit the memory of ancestors, spirits, animals and natural phenomena. Religion remains closely tied to the visible world and to the forces that govern the North.

Travel and combat

The Lossoth excel at movement across snow, tracking, survival, weather observation and the use of equipment suited to cold. Their weapons remain functional: spears, javelins, bows, knives and hunting tools predominate. Mobility and knowledge of terrain matter more than heavy armour.

Place in character creation

A Lossoth character is defined first by community, hunting territory and relationship with the Far North. A journey south represents an enormous change: abundant timber, permanent roads, cities and mild climates often seem as strange to them as the pack ice does to a Gondorian.

Starting Languages

  • Labba — Spoken 8 / Written 0
  • Westron — Spoken 4 / Written 2
  • Sindarin — Spoken 4 / Written 2

Le froid n’est pas un simple décor mais une donnée permanente de la vie. Les vêtements, la nourriture, l’organisation des déplacements et la répartition des tâches sont pensés pour éviter toute dépense inutile de chaleur ou d’énergie.

Apparence et adaptation

Les Lossoth sont généralement robustes et compacts, avec des traits adaptés à un climat extrême. Leurs vêtements superposent peaux, fourrures et cuir afin de protéger le corps du vent et de l’humidité. Leur endurance face au froid est remarquable, tandis que les climats très chauds leur sont beaucoup moins familiers.

Chasse, pêche et élevage

La chasse, la pêche et le piégeage assurent l’essentiel des ressources. Les Lossoth exploitent la viande, les peaux, les os et la graisse avec très peu de gaspillage. Les chiens et les rennes occupent une place importante dans certaines communautés pour le transport, la traction ou l’élevage.

Le savoir pratique vaut autant que la force : suivre une piste après une chute de neige, construire rapidement un abri, conserver de la nourriture ou traverser une étendue gelée sont des compétences ordinaires.

Société et traditions

La famille et le groupe de survie priment sur les institutions complexes. Les anciens sont respectés pour leur mémoire des hivers, des migrations et des lieux sûrs. La parole donnée et l’entraide ont un poids particulier dans un environnement où l’isolement peut être mortel.

Les récits, chants et croyances transmettent la mémoire des ancêtres, des esprits, des animaux et des phénomènes naturels. La religion reste étroitement liée au monde visible et aux forces qui gouvernent le Nord.

Voyage et combat

Les Lossoth excellent dans le déplacement sur neige, le pistage, la survie, l’observation météorologique et l’utilisation d’équipements adaptés au froid. Leurs armes restent fonctionnelles : lances, javelots, arcs, couteaux et outils de chasse dominent. La mobilité et la connaissance du terrain comptent davantage qu’une armure lourde.

Place dans la création de personnage

Un personnage Lossoth est d’abord défini par sa communauté, son territoire de chasse et sa relation au Grand Nord. Un voyage vers le Sud constitue un changement considérable : abondance de bois, routes permanentes, villes et climats doux lui paraissent souvent aussi étranges que la banquise l’est à un Gondorien.

Lossoth

The Lossoth are the Men of the Far North who dwell around the Bay of Forochel. Their Culture was shaped in a land of tundra, snow, ice and violent winds where survival depends on intimate knowledge of the seasons, animals and movement across frozen ground. They belong to the Humans — Hildor Race and remain one of the peoples best adapted to the polar conditions of Middle-earth.

The Far North

Lossoth communities live according to the rhythm of freezing weather, animal migrations and the availability of resources. Camps, shelters and routes change with the seasons; families know how to recognise load-bearing snow, dangerous ice, signs of a storm and areas where game or fuel can be found.

Cold is not merely a background feature but a permanent condition of life. Clothing, food, the organisation of travel and the division of tasks are all designed to avoid wasting heat or energy.

Appearance and adaptation

The Lossoth are generally sturdy and compact, with features adapted to an extreme climate. Their clothing layers hides, fur and leather to protect the body from wind and moisture. Their endurance against cold is remarkable, while very hot climates are far less familiar to them.

Hunting, fishing and husbandry

Hunting, fishing and trapping provide most resources. The Lossoth use meat, hides, bones and fat with very little waste. Dogs and reindeer hold an important place in some communities for transport, hauling or herding.

Practical knowledge matters as much as strength: following a trail after snowfall, rapidly building shelter, preserving food or crossing a frozen expanse are ordinary skills.

Society and traditions

Family and the survival group take precedence over complex institutions. Elders are respected for their memory of winters, migrations and safe places. Keeping one's word and mutual aid carry particular weight in an environment where isolation can be deadly.

Stories, songs and beliefs transmit the memory of ancestors, spirits, animals and natural phenomena. Religion remains closely tied to the visible world and to the forces that govern the North.

Travel and combat

The Lossoth excel at movement across snow, tracking, survival, weather observation and the use of equipment suited to cold. Their weapons remain functional: spears, javelins, bows, knives and hunting tools predominate. Mobility and knowledge of terrain matter more than heavy armour.

Place in character creation

A Lossoth character is defined first by community, hunting territory and relationship with the Far North. A journey south represents an enormous change: abundant timber, permanent roads, cities and mild climates often seem as strange to them as the pack ice does to a Gondorian.
